generatedFrom: Boston and Cambridge public OBJ/GIS sources, OpenStreetMap for Somerville, Brookline, Chelsea, Everett, Medford, Malden and Melrose, MassGIS assessor parcels for the northern house forms, USGS 3DEP bare-earth DEM
buildingPlacement: Original Back Bay normalization retained. Boston catalogue ground values interpreted as metres and Cambridge ground values as feet; primary source floors seated to DEM; geometrically supported upper parts share parent translation. OpenStreetMap footprints extruded by tagged height or levels with type defaults. Per-building normalization audit stored in each tile header (norm field).

restoredWaterCrossings.method: Original source path intervals missing from packaged roads, predominantly within mapped water with shoreline tolerance, bounded by retained road endpoints; freeway and tunnel exclusions retained
restoredWaterCrossings.harvardDeck: 16 m basin pavement with a 10 m Boston street landing, per-point tapered widths, shared endpoint tangents; one linear Boston approach across the three shore pieces, retaining the graded street landing and basin deck

cambridgeApproach.method: Retained OSM horizontal alignments; extend the basin deck above Memorial Drive and grade connected approaches to unchanged outer terrain landings. One-lane slips use 5 m pavement with flared junction mouths; divided Massachusetts Avenue forks widen through overlapping full-width junction mouths. Estimated game profile, not surveyed elevations.

cambridgeTerrain.method: Fixed-anchor Memorial underpass plane with harmonic shoulder; upper roads excluded

longfellowUTurn.method: Source endpoint and interior-vertex junctions share their parent deck heights; water classification cannot lift the junction independently.

terrain.method: Source negative-level profiles with fixed ground anchors; local terrain clamp and preserved upper street decks

leverett.method: Active OSM Leverett Connector paths from unchanged survey mouths to existing municipal street landings; estimated continuous profiles beneath the upper surveyed viaduct

chelseaCreekConnections.method: Complete OSM creek alignments between retained Boston street landings and exact Chelsea street nodes; remove duplicate clipped source pieces, add traffic coverage and estimated smooth bridge deck profiles.
chelseaCreekConnections.heightAccuracy: Estimated game profile with a 4.8 m rise above the higher street landing; not surveyed clearance or movable bridge operation.

tobinBridge.method: Shared double-deck axis on OSM lower roadway; 1525 ft Big Mystic three-span cantilever with 800 ft main span, 439 ft Little Mystic truss, positions anchored to official hydro shore crossings. Deck elevation, deck separation and road grades are original game estimates. Mapped Boston ramp and tunnel alignments are represented as open terrain-adjusted access decks; this does not model the deep tunnel network or reproduce engineering profiles. Chelsea motorway continuation stops at the connected Fourth Street exit and Everett Avenue entrance. Two explicit Boston source-building clearance zones raise the open access interpretation over surveyed roof shells rather than cutting or hiding the buildings.

streetSurfaces.method: Roadway edges measured every 1 m from each surface centerline to the nearest curb within half the nominal width plus 12 m, driveway tongues under 7 m suppressed, gaps to 40 m interpolated, unmeasured stretches ramped to the nominal width; sidewalk inventory polygons grown 0.35 m and clipped to tiles, a polygon mostly in parkland that holds a disc 12 m across (wider than four declared widths) reduced to its declared width (2.9 m when blank) along the boundary; OpenStreetMap service roads measured to the surveyed curbs within half their tagged or class width (4.5 m default) plus 6 m, an unmeasured side completed to the median curb-to-curb width of that line, with surface parking lots and the closed curb faces a service road enters or a lot covers (up to 6000 m2), dissolved and cut around inventory sidewalks; other closed curb faces without a centerline or building filled with concrete when outside parks and inventory sidewalks and under 400 m2 or 3.5 m wide; town curbs regenerated from one pavement union across the towns with 3 m fillets, and cut along a street that a town record gave up to a Boston one (provenance.sourceCopies) on each side where Boston's survey has a curb at 50% or more of the record's stations within its pavement grown by the fillet radius, the surveyed curbs there kept though they lie inside the town; in Everett, Medford, Malden and Melrose a driveway lane laid out from the assessor parcel of each generated house (house_driveways.py: the wider side yard, 2.6 to 3.2 m wide, 0.6 m off the wall, from behind the 2.9 m sidewalk band to the garage door or the back corner of the house, on the parcel and clear of other buildings, none where an OpenStreetMap service road reaches the parcel) joins the driveway fills, the town curb cut across its mouth; Boston curb stretches of 8 m or more lying in parkland (parks grown 3 m) beyond the measuring reach of every street, service road (8 m) and lot (4 m) dropped as remnants of removed roadways, with the inventory sidewalk parts beyond that reach, in parkland and mostly within 5 m of such a stretch; a centerline running inside a park with a curb within 3 m on the park boundary moved onto the roadway 2.5 m beyond that curb (or to the middle of a narrower roadway ending at the next curb), tapering over 12 m with its endpoints fixed, before measuring, where that leaves fewer such stations (the source line kept as sourcePoints); a station such a move cannot take out of the park paved between that curb and the next curb beyond it on the same side (the nominal width past the curb without one), never interpolated from or floored by its neighbours; records of other tiles sharing the roadway at a crosswalk station (8 m along the line from each end of a road tile-builder.ts stripes, 18 m or longer, 7 m wide, not an alley: an edge crossing the station's across line within 40 m, running within cosine 0.8 of the road) copied into that tile as border records.

waterCrossingDecks.method: One deck surface per water-crossing chain of lifted nodes: the inverse-distance blend of the chain's own at-grade junction heights along the chain, each junction raised as far as the terrain and water under the deck, the terrain under its ramps and any road crossing beneath need on its side; ramps keep their pinned ground landings and never sink into the terrain
waterCrossingDecks.heightAccuracy: Estimated game profiles, not surveyed bridge decks

landApproaches.method: A single elevated piece whose lifted end is a node where a terrain road ends and continues it, with nothing crossing beneath, meets the ground there and is re-profiled as a ramp held over the terrain, or becomes a surface street when that leaves it within the at-grade margin everywhere; an elevated piece sinking more than the sink margin into the terrain between its fixed ends is held over it point by point and the held profile pulled taut (its upper concave envelope); declared clipped town ramps get their source tail back and snap to the Boston segment end it reaches; generic connected decks use a shared grade envelope, fixed ground landings and dedicated joins, and terrain/lower-road clearance bounds; infeasible components are reported without moving their landings
landApproaches.heightAccuracy: Estimated game profiles, not surveyed structures

museumRoadConnections.method: Complete three clipped survey mouths on retained GIS approach alignments. Profiles retain the existing game survey datum, with estimated raised approaches and street landings; not surveyed engineering or a reconstruction of underground staging. North branch joins the restored eastbound approach 25 m before the clipped GIS branch origin, allowing a continuous grade at the existing model height. Only the last 45 m of each horizontal approach blends to the measured survey axis. Ambient traffic is excluded while the survey-only highways have no road graph. The raised west approach offsets up to 36 m around the retained Science Park station, and the east approach offsets up to 12 m to separate its rising branch. Street merges follow the terrain until their roadbeds separate.

farMassing.method: Each hidden sprawling complex (not a structure) is followed in far.bin by rectangular fragments: road corridors (pavedWidth or class width) are cut from its ground plan, parts narrower than twice the narrow margin dropped, and each wing's roof height field, sampled on a grid aligned with its dominant wall direction, is covered band by band with greedy largest rectangles

sourceCopies.method: A street that both sources carry keeps one record: a surface OpenStreetMap town road lying within the reach of surface Boston segments all along its own length and running their way leaves the package, then a Boston segment lying the same way along the town roads still there (the stub of a town street); a copy stays, held, when a road meets it at a vertex the record it copies does not have

clippedWaterSpans.method: Stretches of OpenStreetMap ways that the district clipping dropped (MassGIS town outlines stop at the shores of the tidal rivers), restored as deck pieces where they form one path between two dangling road ends and cross mapped water; deck roads they join get a lifted joining end so the water-crossing step levels each bridge as one chain

townSeams.method: OpenStreetMap streets that the district clipping split at a line between two towns (neighbouring town outlines leave slivers and overlaps, and pieces under 3 m are dropped), each dangling end near a shared edge carried along its source way, and the ways continuing from its end node, to the first package road the path meets: that road's end, or a vertex inserted into it for a junction; overlapping pieces of one way cut back to the middle of the overlap

bridgeJoints.method: Two deck pieces of one OpenStreetMap bridge meeting at ground level within the zone of a shared town edge, with no other road at the joint: the joint lifted and both pieces given the straight line between their outer ends

edgeBridges.method: An OpenStreetMap deck piece ending at ground level at the edge of the districts with no other road there and a steeper average grade than the limit (a bridge the edge of the map cuts mid-span): it and the deck pieces joined to it through lifted joints back to the ground landing held level at the landing height, the edge end lifted

northOverpasses.method: Lower streets cut to the design clearance under source decks (level beneath the deck, ramping along the street network, walled beyond the corridor), other street corridors kept and deck ends carried over the trench edge on approach pieces; valley-crossing streets carried at the rim level on decks and filled approaches; buildings and lower roads under fills fixed; original vertices, deck profiles and streets recorded for replay
northOverpasses.heightAccuracy: Estimated game profiles, not surveyed structures

i93North.method: OpenStreetMap I 93 carriageways and motorway_link ramps from the cached town extracts, resampled with source vertices kept; decks solved as smoothing splines over the graded terrain with street and water clearances above and overpass clearances beneath; graded grid cut under the overpasses (street corridors and buildings kept); concrete closures inside the Medford/Stoneham coverage edge; southbound lower deck held beneath the surveyed Charlestown viaduct onto the Zakim, with the City Square ramp pieces it replaces cut from the survey mesh; survey traces joining the Central Artery tunnel bores and the Cross Street entrance to the decks for traffic and GPS

bostonHighways.method: Boston GIS layer 8 segments of the Massachusetts Turnpike, Storrow Drive and their ramps in travel order, resampled with source vertices kept; profiles solved as smoothing splines over the graded terrain with street and water clearances above and overpass clearances beneath, the street bridges over the cut levelled between their landings first (a street the segments start at level 0 on a bridge node over the road taken as that bridge's ramp); stretches below source level 0, under a reviewed tunnel span or under a building, and cuts walled at the pavement edge, kept as tunnel records with their covered intervals, every other stretch a deck with the grid cut under it; the survey's cut closed under each building over a road, passages recorded for building_passages.py where a ramp cannot pass under a base, structures standing in the roadway removed; ramps matched to their carriageway at the gore and landed on the graded street vertex, or on the Central Artery tunnel road they join, and a deck split where a street joins it at its height; concrete closures inside the Newton coverage edge
